title: Compatibility guardrails and pinning exceptions for experimental inbound open models
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Purpose: provide a lightweight, prescriptive set of compatibility guardrails for new inbound open-model submissions that are flagged as 'experimental' and may be exempt from immediate full-version pinning. This ticket clarifies requirements, decision logic, and acceptance criteria for PM + Runtime + Research to accept or reject an experimental inbound model into the catalog without full pinning, while preserving safety and predictable runtime behavior.

Background: Teams have repeatedly requested a faster path to list experimental community models so customers can discover and test them, but past admissions without clear runtime metadata caused unexpected fallbacks and degraded SLOs. We need a small, auditable decision path that allows limited exemptions to the default "pin at major version" rule when safe, and encodes compensating controls (traffic caps, canary channels, automatic compatibility probes).

Goals:
- Define minimal compatibility metadata required for an experimental exception (format/schema, runtime hints).
- Specify automated probes and pass/fail thresholds used by intake to assign an 'experimental-exempt' flag.
- Define runtime fallback mapping and measurable SLOs for exempt models.
- Establish rollout and deprecation rules for exempt models (timebox, telemetry gates).

Scope (in):
- Intake schema additions and validation checks in the catalog gateway.
- Runtime probe suite (sanity tokenization, KV signature check, sample latency profile) for experimental-exempt candidates.
- Decision rubric used by PM/reviewers to grant temporary exemption.
- Console UI annotations and a webhook to signal exemption state to customers.

Out of scope:
- Full model quantization recommendations and kernel tuning (Runtime will continue iterative work separately).
- Long-term pinning policy changes for GA models.

Success metrics:
- 0 critical runtime regressions caused by experimental-exempt models in first 30 days after admission (regression = >5% error spike or >2x latency p95 vs baseline).
- 80% of experimental admissions either graduate to pinned variant or are retired within their 90-day timebox.
- Intake decision turnaround under 48 hours for 90% of submissions using the new flow.
proposed_solution: Add a boolean field 'experimental_exempt' to intake metadata with required supporting hints: 'expected_seq_len', 'kv_shape_signature', 'compat_flags' (list of strings), and 'runtime_risk_tier' (low/medium/high).

Implement an automated probe pipeline: tokenization sanity, KV shape verification, 10 synthetic traces for cold and warm KV-cache to estimate p50/p95, and a lightweight correctness smoke test (prompt set of 30 items).

Define a Decision Rubric: automated probes must pass (see acceptance criteria). If probes fail, intake is rejected. If pass, PM + Runtime perform a manual 1-hour review and can grant a 90-day exemption with traffic caps and console annotation.

Runtime fallback policy: map 'experimental_exempt' to a constrained deployment route with autoscaling disabled, capped QPS, and automatic fallback to the nearest compatible pinned variant. Fallback must be logged and surfaced in Console.
Telemetry: surface per-model exemption state, traffic fraction, probe pass/fail history, and regression alerts to the Console and on the intake PR comment.
acceptance_criteria: Intake schema accepts 'experimental_exempt' and required hints; schema validation errors return actionable messages.
Automated probe pipeline runs end-to-end in CI for submitted model bundles and reports a structured pass/fail result within 30 minutes.
A granted exemption automatically creates a constrained serving route with caps and explicit console annotation indicating: exemption start, expiry date, reason, and reviewer initials.
Fallback mapping resolves to a compatible pinned variant when any runtime probe exceeds thresholds; each fallback increments a model-level fallback counter surfaced in Console.
Documentation: concise PRD + reviewer checklist published in Confluence and linked from intake UI; sample unblock playbook for common probe failures is present.
30-day post-admission monitoring: no critical SLO violations attributable to the exempt model in the first 30 days (metric queries and alerts pre-configured).
Manual audit trail: every exemption decision is logged to the catalog ledger (intake ticket ID + reviewer notes) and exposed via the intake webhook.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Experimental models could degrade platform SLOs if traffic exceeds expectations. Mitigation: strict default caps, autoscale disabled, and automatic emergency rollback trigger based on latency/error rate thresholds.

Risk: Ingress without clear compatibility metadata leads to unpredictable runtime kernel selection. Mitigation: make 'kv_shape_signature' and 'expected_seq_len' mandatory for exemptions; probe fails block admission.
Risk: Reviewer subjectivity leads to inconsistent approvals. Mitigation: require automated probe pass and a short standardized reviewer checklist; keep decisions auditable.
